decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up approach to the right end of the set square, gradually orienting the open gripper downward; left arm stays at origin.
Continue above the ruler's right section with open fingers, pitching toward a vertical grasp while keeping ample reach margin.
Move above the ruler, finishing the downward approach before turning the jaws across its narrow width; avoid the cubes.
Finish pointing the gripper down above the right end, remaining clear of the tabletop and blocks.
Rotate the downward open jaws above the ruler so their closing direction will span its narrow width.
Continue aligning the jaws across the ruler and descend slowly, checking the right wrist view before contact.
Complete transverse jaw alignment and lower gradually toward a pinch on the right section of the set square, not on a cube.
The downward motion met resistance near tabletop height. Ease up slightly, correct tilt, and close around the ruler; retention remains to be checked visually.
With the ruler pinched, rotate it gently in the tabletop plane toward a horizontal straightedge. Keep cube contact strictly planar and check that the ruler follows.
The ruler followed only partly. Seat the pinch a few millimeters and make a small planar advance and turn to assess coupling, without approaching cube tops.
Advance the ruler's right end along the table to remove its remaining diagonal angle. Keep the grasp closed and height fixed.
Bring the right end nearly level with the left. Begin a separate left-workspace approach to stabilize the other end for an even tabletop push.
Hold the level ruler with the right arm while approaching its left end from above in the left workspace.
Continue the left gripper's overhead approach with gradual downward pitch; the right hand holds the ruler without advancing it.
Finish the left downward pitch while advancing above the ruler's left section, keeping both elbows up and the right end stationary.
Rotate the left jaws across the ruler while centering above its left end. Keep the right grasp stationary and the tool on the table.
Continue left jaw rotation above the ruler and descend slightly toward its grasp height. Both hands remain outside the cube row.
Finish orienting the left jaws normal to the straightedge and settle to the same low grasp height used at the right end.
Close the left fingers around the ruler's left section with a small centering adjustment. Keep both ends low and verify the tool before pushing.
Push both ends forward together at fixed height so the straightedge gathers the cubes into a common row without lifting them.
All three now meet the straightedge. Apply a short, even final tabletop push to square their faces before withdrawing and resetting.
The cube faces appear aligned. Withdraw the straightedge evenly along the tabletop to leave clearance before releasing and returning both arms to origin.
Release the straightedge on the tabletop, then lift only the empty grippers clear. The three blocks remain visibly in a straight row.
Begin resetting both empty arms along separated elbow-up paths, withdrawing from the aligned blocks while unwinding wrist yaw.
Continue the collision-free reset, keeping empty open grippers above and behind the ruler as wrist rotations unwind.
Complete wrist-yaw reset behind the objects, keeping translation small enough for joint-continuous elbow-up motion.
Pitch the empty grippers back toward their initial orientation while retracting both arms toward their own origins, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Continue gradual return to the initial poses with open, empty grippers; the aligned blocks and released ruler remain undisturbed.
Continue the final reset approach, reducing wrist pitch and retracting smoothly without changing elbow configuration or contacting the objects.
Approach both recorded origin poses with reduced increments, preserving joint continuity and keeping the object row untouched.
